overview: A weak system brings light snow to the Cascades and Sierra this weekend. A stronger system arrives in the Sierra and Cascades around Tuesday, with a break on Monday. The Weather Prediction Center expects a wet pattern for Northern California and the Pacific Northwest next week.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: A weak system brings light snow to the mountains from Saturday evening into Sunday, and the main showers stay offshore. Snow is mostly light. Monday brings a short break. A stronger system arrives Tuesday with snow in the mountains and rain mixing in at lower elevations, and it lingers into Wednesday. Mt. Baker and Stevens Pass have the best totals for the week, with Mt. Baker at 15" and Stevens Pass at 11".

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: A weak system crosses Sunday, bringing light snow above about 4,000 feet and light rain in the valleys. The National Weather Service expects little snow. A break comes Monday before a stronger storm arrives midweek, with rain in the valleys and snow in the mountains. Sugar Bowl shows the most snow for the week at 13", and the Sierra forecasters expect the midweek storm to be wetter and windier than the last one.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Snow turns to flurries in the Coast Mountains through Monday. Rain and showers arrive Tuesday and Wednesday, so snow totals stay modest. Whistler has the most for the week at 15", with most of it falling early in the week.

regions.title: Eastern Sierra
regions.text: Cold, clear nights bring freezing fog to the valleys Saturday night. A fast-moving system brings snow to the Sierra Sunday, with limited moisture and little accumulation. Monday afternoon through Tuesday evening is the best travel window before a stronger storm arrives midweek with more snow. Mammoth expects 9" for the week, with the heaviest snow Wednesday.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
